correctness.rationale: Every nonzero singular \(2\times2\) matrix has rank one and is determined up to \(q-1\) nonzero scalars by its image line \(L\) and kernel line \(K\). For types \((L,K)\), \((L',K')\), adjacency is exactly \(L'=K\) or \(L=K'\). One diagonal representative per projective line gives a dominating set of size \(q+1\). For \(q>2\), the support-deficit rectangle argument forces any hypothetical support below \(q+1\) into the equality pattern where a selected off-diagonal type has no selected type-neighbor; because its fiber has at least two scalar copies, an unselected copy remains undominated. For \(q=2\), fibers are singletons and the displayed two projective types dominate all nine vertices, while no vertex is universal. Independent finite reconstruction of the actual \(q=2,3\) matrix graphs agrees with \(2\) and \(4\).
correctness.risk: The projective-fiber lower bound is specific to matrix size \(2\); higher dimensions have more complicated rank strata.

final_claim: For the simple undirected zero-divisor graph on the nonzero singular matrices of \(M_2(\mathbb F_q)\), with distinct \(A,B\) adjacent when \(AB=0\) or \(BA=0\), the domination number is \(2\) for \(q=2\) and \(q+1\) for every \(q>2\).
limitations: No formula is claimed for \(M_n(\mathbb F_q)\) with \(n\ge3\).
